name: Nico Collins

background.fact: Born March 19, 1999; born and raised in Pinson, Alabama, the youngest of three children. He went to Clay-Chalkville High School, whose football team won the 2014 Class 6A state championship.
In high school he caught 60 passes for 1,103 yards and 16 touchdowns as a junior and 43 for 865 and 9 touchdowns as a senior; he committed to Michigan in February 2017 over Georgia and Alabama.
At Michigan he had a breakout 2018 (38 catches, 632 yards, 6 touchdowns, Most Improved Offensive Player) and a career-best 165 yards and three touchdowns against Indiana on November 23, 2019.
Houston took him in the third round (pick 89) of the 2021 draft. Listed at 6 ft 4 in, 222 lb, age 27, in his sixth NFL season, jersey 12.
Career regular season: 72 games, 317 catches, 4,731 yards, 28 touchdowns. Best years were 2023 (1,297 yards, 8 touchdowns) and 2025 (1,117 yards, 6 touchdowns on 120 targets).

family.fact: His father, Don Collins, a Michigan native, worked as a surgical tech and his mother worked in human resources; his paternal grandparents live near Buffalo, New York.
Nothing about a spouse, partner or children was found in the reachable sources: not found.

scouts_read: Collins appears healthy and should play a normal share of snaps, so the question is targets, not availability. He has seen only 4 to 5 targets in each of his last three games while Schultz, Hutchinson and Boutte split the rest, and his 2026 average is 10.6 points. Houston is a 4.5 point favorite in a game with a modest total near 40, and Cleveland is about average against receivers, so there is no big matchup boost. Touchdowns are what move his score, and a preview that calls Cleveland's red zone defense poor gives some upside there. I would project roughly 8 to 12 points, with a 20 point game possible if he scores twice and a single digit game likely if the targets stay low.
